scenes.headline: How Prime serves a giant model to long-running agents
scenes.sub: Prefill and decode apart, and four fixes to the KV cache.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ravioli! Here's how Prime Intellect serves G L M five point three to coding agents.

scenes.text: Agent turns resend a huge history plus a short new tail, so serving them is mostly about where the KV cache lives and how it moves.
scenes.say: An agent turn resends a huge history plus a short new tail. Serving agents is mostly about the cache.

scenes.title: Prefill and decode on separate GPUs

steps.say: A turn arrives. A router sends it to the prefill worker that already holds most of its history.
Prefill runs on its own eight GPUs. Older history comes back from a cache tier in host memory.
Then a decoder pulls the finished cache across. Decode never stops to run a prefill.
One prefill group feeding four decoders served the most sessions at the speed target.

scenes.title: Why the prefill group is data-parallel

left.title: Tensor-parallel attention
items: The MLA latent has no head axis
So every GPU keeps a full copy
left.say: Split attention by heads, and every GPU still needs the whole cached latent. So each keeps a full copy.

right.title: Data-parallel attention
right.say: Give each GPU its own requests, and each cache exists once. About five times the usable cache.

scenes.title: One cache row, in four bits

parts.note: the 512-value latent at four bits each
parts.say: The latent, packed at four bits a value.

parts.note: the rope part, kept in FP8
parts.say: The positional part, left at eight bits.
Three hundred fifty-two bytes, not five hundred seventy-six. About half again as many tokens fit.

scenes.say: Decode keeps copies for speed, so Prime shrank each one.

scenes.credit: Prime Intellect's post, KV layout figure

steps.say: Moving the cache had its own problem. Layer-major storage cuts one block into a small copy per layer.
Block-major puts every layer of a block together. One block, one copy.

scenes.title: Descriptors to move the same KV
scenes.say: With blocks sixteen times smaller, block-major needed ten times fewer copies, and transfers got nearly twice as fast.

scenes.text: A latent cache is small, but every tensor-parallel rank keeps all of it. Topology, format and layout are cache decisions.
scenes.mark: every tensor-parallel rank keeps all of it

recap: Prefill and decode on separate GPUs
Data-parallel prefill keeps one cache copy
scenes.say: To recap: split prefill from decode, keep one copy of each cache, and shrink and batch what moves.
